ac-twice: The main-failing branch of ac-twice says neither task is sent back. Task A's check run ends before task B's, and at that point the test is unlisted, so FR-7 holds the failure against A and sends A back. The twice rule only re-runs the test on main during B's gate, after A is already back.

What the Hub does now: lists the test as failing on main, does not send B back, re-judges A's run as preexisting, and adds a note on A saying the failure is now listed.

Making A 'not sent back' means undoing the send-back, and that needs two contract changes the approved design does not cover:
1. A revision_needed -> completed transition. Today only in_progress and rejected leave revision_needed (hub/hub/task_transitions.py:147).
2. Un-holding the evidence the checks send-back held. There is no review decision for 'back to awaiting' (EVIDENCE_REVIEW_DECISIONS = accepted, rejected, held), and review rows are append-only.

Going through in_progress -> completed as the operator would record a fake operator completion and leave A's evidence held, so approving A would merge nothing.

Options for the operator:
(a) Amend ac-twice to: A is re-judged and noted, B is not sent back.
(b) Approve a follow-up change that adds a Hub-only undo of a checks send-back, including restoring its evidence.

acceptance_criteria: ac-whole: Given a fixture project seeded with at least one item of every listed kind, when the thread is fully opened, then every seeded item appears exactly once

ac-surface: Given two documents with three hand-made tasks and a conversation recorded between them, when the surface is shown, then it shows document, one folded knot of four items naming its span, document — in that order

ac-recursive: Given a document with an approved task whose run recorded evidence that was accepted and merged, when the reader opens document, then task, then run, then closes the task, then each level shows the listed children in time order, and after closing the task knot is in view

ac-face: Given the surface of this repository's project, when the page is rendered, then every knot shows glyph, kind word, title, date or span and actors, and no text on the page matches an id pattern (tsk-, run-, spdoc-, fct-) or a snake_case event name
ac-links: Given a run knot, when its link is followed, then the run's transcript opens
ac-faithful: Given a fixture project whose records carry known timestamps, when the feed is walked, then every knot names at least one stored record and siblings are in non-decreasing recorded time
ac-fold: Given a task with six consecutive runs and then a merge, when the task knot is opened, then one folded knot reads six runs, followed by the merge knot unfolded
ac-scale: Given a trial-Hub project seeded with 10,000 items, when the tab is opened, the beginning is jumped to, and a knot is opened, then each shows content within one second

tasks.notes:
QA review at 2cdd5b8 — approved.

Checked:
1. Tests: `py -3.11 -m pytest tests/test_pull_the_thread_feed.py -q` (in hub/) gives 11 passed. That matches every evidence row.
2. Code read: hub/hub/project_thread.py and hub/hub/api/v1/thread.py. The route is registered under /projects/{id}/thread.
   - FR-3: each item gets exactly one parent, the first one that exists. The ac-whole test seeds every kind and checks that every record is reached exactly once.
   - FR-4: group_surface handles the surface, and ac-surface asserts document, a group of 4, then document.
   - FR-5: levels are document → task → run, and evidence sits under its run. Opening and closing a level is the same read.
   - FR-6: plain() and human() strip ids and event names, and every knot is given actors ("Hub" as the fallback).
   - FR-7: run, task, document, evidence, conversation, firing and vault knots all carry a link.
   - FR-8: siblings are sorted by (start, key), and the paging test fails if the order is reversed.
   - FR-9: fold_routine works at every depth, milestones are not routine kinds, and the 6-runs-then-merge test passes.
   - FR-12: the 10k test stays under 1s.
3. Drive on real data: I built the feed with this checkout's code against a copy of the trial Hub database (project proj-d85a82bf4216, 5,572 records) and walked every level.
   - Each record was reached exactly once (5,572 unique), and no level was out of order.
   - No knot lacks a time, and every knot has actors.
   - None of the 3,000 ancestor chains I checked failed to reach its knot.
   - The build took 0.14s.
   - Face scan: no tsk-/run-/spdoc-/fct- ids. The only snake_case hits are code words that task and question titles quote themselves (e.g. "depends_on"), not event names.

Accepted the evidence for FR-3/4/5/6/7/8/9/12 at the feed level. The browser parts of the how_to_checks for FR-5/6/7/12 (rendered page, transcript opening, timed tab) are carried by task-b0c1dd334579 and task-3e9661e4d53b.

Side note (not grounds for revision): on this commit, /thread/knot ancestors for a surface item inside a routine fold inside a surface group stops at the group and leaves out the inner fold. I reproduced this with 5 loose firings: ancestors(firing) = [group], and the group's level shows only the inner fold. That is the addressable requirement, which another task owns, and task-41ba61cbff84's branch says it fixes it in _parent_of. Verify it there.

requirement_links.latest_rejection_reason: QA review at 22d4f8919e4d. Ran hub/tests/test_pull_the_thread_feed.py: 9 passed. Two defects send it back (fixes added to the spec as tasks): (1) FR-3/FR-9/FR-5 -- a routine fold inside a surface group cannot be opened: the fold key 'fold:fold:surface|x|x' is parsed back to parent 'fold:surface', so it reports child_count 0, GET /thread?under=<it> answers 404, and its members never appear. Repro: one document plus five firings of a job with no loop; the walk reaches only the document (task-41ba61cbff84). (2) FR-6 -- on this repository's surface, 155 of 160 knots have no actors (every document knot), and 516 knots have none across the whole thread (firings ignore the job's agent; merges and tasks with null actors) (task-6f1c338db709). Also the ac-whole fixture leaves out a vault addition and a document merge, both kinds FR-3 lists; this is folded into the first fix task. Evidence: FR-4 (surface grouping), FR-7 (links), FR-8 (faithful order) and FR-12 (scale) held in what I ran, but they are rejected with this verdict because they come from the same commit. Expect them to hold again after the fix.

acceptance_criteria: ac-present: Given a project with history spanning more than a month, when the Thread tab is opened, then 'jump to the beginning' is used, then 'back to the present', then the newest surface knot is in view first, then the oldest, then the newest again

ac-recursive: Given a document with an approved task whose run recorded evidence that was accepted and merged, when the reader opens document, then task, then run, then closes the task, then each level shows the listed children in time order, and after closing the task knot is in view

ac-face: Given the surface of this repository's project, when the page is rendered, then every knot shows glyph, kind word, title, date or span and actors, and no text on the page matches an id pattern (tsk-, run-, spdoc-, fct-) or a snake_case event name

ac-access: Given the Thread tab with reduced motion enabled, using only the keyboard, when the reader moves to a knot, opens it and closes it, then every step works, no animation runs, and knot kinds remain distinguishable in a greyscale screenshot

ac-visual: Given the mock of the Thread page in light and dark, fed recorded fixtures, when the operator looks at it, opens knots, and watches the thread draw, then the operator judges that it reads as the identity's red thread and approves the look before the tab is wired in

tasks.notes:
QA review at eae0db71d886. Approved. All four pieces of evidence (FR-2, FR-5, FR-6, FR-13) are accepted as partial: the components are proven in the mock, not yet in the wired tab.

What I ran in the review checkout:
- `npm ci` in hub/ui.
- `npx vitest run src/__tests__/Thread.test.tsx`: 3/3 passed.
- eslint on the new files: 0 errors and 1 warning (react-refresh in mock/thread-main.tsx, harmless).
- `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in the thread files.
- Started the mock server (`vite --config vite.mock.config.ts` on :5199) and ran `py -3.11 mock/drive_thread.py`: all 23 checks passed.
  - present: newest knot in view, then oldest, then newest.
  - recursive: document (12 children) > task (23) > run (3), each in the recorded order; the task stays in view after closing.
  - face: glyph, word, title and when on every knot; no ids or event names.
  - access: reduced motion leaves animation-name `none` everywhere; Tab, arrow keys, Enter and Space all work.

Independent checks of the fixture (my own script):
- All 25 recorded levels are sorted by start time.
- All 163 surface knots, and every knot at every level, carry actors.
- No knot word, title or actor matches an id pattern.
- The one snake_case hit is the human task title "Teach depends_on…". That is content, not an event name.

I looked at the screenshots: light with a document opened, and dark with reduced motion in greyscale. The madder line, the beads, and the glyph-plus-word kind column all read well.

Limits:
- The recorded history spans 6–23 Oct, less than the month ac-present asks for, and nothing ran against a live Hub. The acceptance drive (task-3e9661e4d53b) and the wired tab (task-b0c1dd334579) cover those.
- ac-visual is still the operator's call.

Small side note: mock/README.md says the last drive's screenshots are "committed in mock/thread-shots/", but `*.png` is gitignored (.gitignore:80), so they are not in the commit. The screenshots must be sent to the operator separately.

tasks.title: The Thread tab in the app

acceptance_criteria: ac-tab: Given two projects on the trial Hub, when the operator opens the Thread tab of each, then the tab sits right after Overview and each shows only its own project's knots

ac-present: Given a project with history spanning more than a month, when the Thread tab is opened, then 'jump to the beginning' is used, then 'back to the present', then the newest surface knot is in view first, then the oldest, then the newest again

ac-recursive: Given a document with an approved task whose run recorded evidence that was accepted and merged, when the reader opens document, then task, then run, then closes the task, then each level shows the listed children in time order, and after closing the task knot is in view

ac-face: Given the surface of this repository's project, when the page is rendered, then every knot shows glyph, kind word, title, date or span and actors, and no text on the page matches an id pattern (tsk-, run-, spdoc-, fct-) or a snake_case event name
ac-links: Given a run knot, when its link is followed, then the run's transcript opens
ac-address: Given the address of a run knot three levels deep, when it is opened in a fresh window, then document, task and run are open, the run knot is in view and has keyboard focus

ac-live: Given the Thread tab open, once at the present end and once scrolled to the beginning, when a task changes status, then its knot appears at the present end within five seconds, and the scrolled-away view does not move
ac-scale: Given a trial-Hub project seeded with 10,000 items, when the tab is opened, the beginning is jumped to, and a knot is opened, then each shows content within one second

ac-access: Given the Thread tab with reduced motion enabled, using only the keyboard, when the reader moves to a knot, opens it and closes it, then every step works, no animation runs, and knot kinds remain distinguishable in a greyscale screenshot

ac-visual: Given the mock of the Thread page in light and dark, fed recorded fixtures, when the operator looks at it, opens knots, and watches the thread draw, then the operator judges that it reads as the identity's red thread and approves the look before the tab is wired in

acceptance_criteria: ac-whole: Given a fixture project seeded with at least one item of every listed kind, when the thread is fully opened, then every seeded item appears exactly once

ac-recursive: Given a document with an approved task whose run recorded evidence that was accepted and merged, when the reader opens document, then task, then run, then closes the task, then each level shows the listed children in time order, and after closing the task knot is in view
ac-fold: Given a task with six consecutive runs and then a merge, when the task knot is opened, then one folded knot reads six runs, followed by the merge knot unfolded
tasks.description: In hub/hub/project_thread.py a fold's key is `fold:{parent_key}|{first member key}`, and Thread.find/_parent_of recover the parent with `key[5:].split('|', 1)[0]`. When the parent is itself a fold (a surface group holding four or more consecutive routine knots, e.g. firings of a job with no loop document, or runs with no task), the inner fold's key is `fold:fold:surface|x|x` and the recovered parent is `fold:surface`, which does not exist. The inner fold then reports child_count 0 and GET /thread?under=<it> answers 404, so its members are unreachable. Make fold keys unambiguous (or resolve the parent another way) so nested folds open, report their count, and appear in /thread/knot ancestors. Add a Hub test: one document plus five firings of a non-loop job; walking the thread reaches all five firings once. Also extend the ac-whole fixture to cover the listed kinds it currently omits: a vault addition and a document merge (SpecDocumentMerge).

ac-controls: Given a new project, when a document is approved with the job at its default, then with button-only, then with a chosen runner and model and the button pressed, then the default shows no button and records no firing; button-only records no firing on approval but one on the press; the press's firing records the chosen runner and model

ac-cost: Given two chapters firings in a project, when the operator looks for their cost in the app, then each firing's tokens (and money where reported) and the project's total for the job are shown, and match what the firings recorded

ac-agent: Given an agent with the job off, when it creates a chapter through its tools, then submits an edit citing a missing record, then the chapter appears on the surface as a version under the agent's name, and the edit is refused

acceptance_criteria: A chapter version citing 1,000 commits of this repo opens its surface in under 1s and every cited commit appears under a release tag
No git argv grows with the number of cited commits
tasks.description: Side finding from QA review of task-298977e55f0e (not in the spec's criteria). chapters.overlay (hub/hub/chapters.py) runs on every GET /projects/{id}/thread, including surface and every level open, and _resolve_shas runs `git rev-parse` once per cited sha. Measured on this repo: 300 cited commits = 8.7s in _resolve_shas + 2.3s in _commit_facts, about 11s per request with nothing cached. Separately, _commit_facts passes every full sha to one `git show` argv: past ~780 shas (40 chars each) that is over the Windows 32,767-char command-line limit, the OSError is swallowed and the chapter silently opens with no commits. Suggested fix: one `git cat-file --batch-check` / `git show --stdin`-style call fed on stdin, and/or a cache keyed on (version id, repo HEAD).

Build the whole "Checks wait less" change in this one task. Read the document first with read_spec_document (path spec/changes/checks-wait-less-fresh-results-after-master-moves-and-checks-scoped-to-the-paths-they-cover/spec.json, include=full): FR-1..FR-9 and their acceptance criteria are the standard. Architect reviews it.

Base: master at or after 31f77f2 (fail-fast checks + inline main baseline in hub/hub/project_checks.py `_MainBaseline`; conftest schema template; `--dist loadgroup`). Build on that, do not undo it.

What to build:
1. FR-1..FR-5 — when a project's main tip changes (the Hub's own integration in hub/hub/task_integration.py, and outside the Hub within 120s), start background check runs for its completed/under_review tasks whose latest result is for another tip, oldest completed first, within MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS. A run still running when main moves is ended (whole process tree), recorded superseded (not failed, not `error`), and replaced. The gate's current-tip rule (`project_checks.view`, requirement_gate.py ~1020-1070) stays strict: a stale green never passes.

requirement_links.statement: When a project's main tip changes, the Hub MUST start a check run, in the background, for every task of that project in completed or under_review whose latest result is not for the new tip, without anyone requesting approval.
A main tip change made outside the Hub (an operator's own merge or push to the main branch) MUST trigger the same refresh within 120 seconds of the change.
A check run still running when its project's main tip changes MUST be ended, recorded as superseded rather than failed, and replaced by a run on the new tip.
Refresh runs SHOULD start in the order their tasks entered completed, oldest first, within the existing limit on concurrent runs.
Approval MUST continue to accept only a result for the current main tip and the current merge targets; a result for an older tip MUST NOT count as passing.
The operator MAY give each check an optional list of path patterns, set in the project's Checks settings and refused from any run credential, as the rest of the check is.
A check with path patterns MUST be skipped when no file changed between the run's main tip and the merged commit matches any of them, and MUST run, as today, when one does or when it has no patterns.

A skipped check MUST be recorded in the run's results as skipped, with the reason that no changed file matched its paths, MUST count as passing at the gate, and MUST appear as skipped (no matching changes) wherever the run's checks are shown, never left out.

The project-checks capability MUST state that a run executes the configured checks in order and stops after the first one that fails on the merged work and passes on main, and that a failure main shares does not stop it.

acceptance_criteria: own-failure-stops: Given a task whose merged work fails the first of two checks, which passes on main, when its check run executes, then the run is failed and the second check was not executed
shared-failure-continues: Given a task whose first check fails on main too, when its check run executes, then the later checks still execute and the failure is recorded pre-existing
skipped-passes: Given a check whose paths match no changed file, when the run executes and approval is requested, then the check is recorded skipped with its reason and the gate counts it as passing
superseded-state: Given a run still executing when the project's main tip moves, when the move is noticed, then the run is recorded superseded, not failed, and does not pass at the gate

requirement_links.statement: A check run SHALL execute the configured checks in order, in a Hub-owned scratch worktree detached at a commit whose tree is the project's main branch tip with every merge target of the task's approval merged in, and SHALL never run in the project's root checkout or an agent's worktree. tasks.title: Wire the loom into the Thread page

acceptance_criteria: ac-mock-match: Given the trial Hub's Thread page for this repository and the mock at mock-loom.html?layout=horizontal&thread=wave, both at 1440x900 with the same chapter selected, in dark and in light, when the two are screenshotted after the draw-in has finished, then the thread's shape, knot positions and sizes, labels, header line and panel layout match, and any difference is limited to agent chip colours or knots the mock's recording does not have

ac-opens-newest: Given a project with 17 chapters and one newer knot not in a chapter, when the operator opens the Thread tab, then the newest surface knot is selected and in view at the right, every knot to its left is older, and the beginning control selects chapter 1
ac-even: Given two neighbouring chapters two months apart and two a day apart, when the thread is drawn, then the horizontal distance between each pair of neighbouring knots is the same

ac-silence: Given two neighbouring surface knots, the second starting 60 days after the first ended, when the thread is drawn, then the stretch between them carries the label '2 months later', and a stretch between knots a day apart carries none

ac-alternate: Given a surface of 5 knots, when the thread is drawn, then the knots sit alternately above and below the middle, each label is on the side away from the middle, and the line is the madder colour

ac-count: Given 17 chapters spanning Mar 7 to Oct 24 and 1 newer conversation not in a chapter, when the page opens, then it reads '17 chapters', 'Mar 7 to Oct 24', and '1 newer knot not in a chapter yet'

ac-panel: Given the chapter 'The mender and the stall alarms' (47 knots, 97 all the way down: 45 conversations, 1 vault entry, 1 document) selected, when the panel shows it, then it reads 'Chapter 17 of 17', the title, the summary, 'Oct 24 · 1 day', '47 knots · 97 all the way down', chips for manager, Operator, mender and Architect, and '45 conversations', '1 vault entry', '1 document'
ac-panel-link: Given a conversation knot selected, when the operator presses 'Open the conversation', then the app opens that conversation, as the old thread's link did
ac-before-after: Given chapter 16 selected, when the operator presses the panel's 'after' control, then chapter 17 is selected, and on chapter 17 the 'after' control is disabled

ac-descend: Given a chapter holding 47 conversations selected, when the operator chooses the third knot on the panel's thread, then the panel describes that conversation as 'Conversation 3 of 47', with a trail naming the chapter, and choosing the chapter in the trail selects the chapter again
ac-leaf: Given a knot that holds nothing selected, when the panel shows it, then the panel's thread shows the knots beside it with it marked as selected

ac-days: Given a chapter stored as 2026-10-24T00:00:00Z to 2026-10-24T23:59:59Z, with the browser in UTC+1 and in UTC-5, when it is shown on the thread and in the panel, then both read 'Oct 24' and the panel reads '1 day'

ac-page-earlier: Given a surface of 165 knots with the newest 40 loaded and the 40th selected, when the reader scrolls to within one screen width of the left end, then the next older page is requested and drawn to the left, the selected knot is unchanged and the knots that were in view stay where they were on screen
ac-scale: Given a project with 10,000 recorded items on the operator's machine, when the Thread tab is opened, and then the beginning control is pressed, then knots show within one second each time

ac-address: Given a run three levels below a chapter selected, and the URL copied, when the URL is opened in a new tab, then that run is selected with a trail of its chapter and the knots between, it is in view on the panel's thread, its chapter is in view on the surface, and it has keyboard focus

ac-live: Given the page open at the beginning of the thread with chapter 1 selected, when an agent's run starts in the project, then within five seconds the new activity is on the thread's present end, and chapter 1 is still selected and still in view

ac-keys: Given chapter 10 focused, when the reader presses Right, then Enter, then Escape, then chapter 11 is selected, then the first knot inside chapter 11, then chapter 11 again, focus following each time
ac-drag: Given the pointer pressed on a knot, when it is dragged 200 pixels left and released, then the thread has scrolled 200 pixels and the selected knot has not changed

ac-reduced: Given the browser set to reduced motion, when the page opens and a knot is chosen, then the thread, knots, labels and panel show at once with no drawing, glint, pulse, rise or glide, and the content is the same as without reduced motion
ac-draws: Given normal motion settings, when the page opens, then the thread is partly drawn from the left a quarter of a second in, and fully drawn with every knot shown within two seconds
ac-weave: Given the chapters job on, when the page opens, then 'Weave the thread' is offered and pressing it asks the job to fire, as before
ac-unreadable: Given the thread route failing, when the page opens, then it says the thread could not be read and to reload
tasks.description: On the trial Hub (:8010, project proj-d85a82bf4216, served from source with this branch's UI), drive the Thread tab in a real browser through every acceptance criterion that a browser can show: screenshots of the page beside the mock (mock-loom.html?layout=horizontal&thread=wave) with the same knot selected, in dark and light; opening at the newest knot, the count line, the panel for a chapter, descending three levels and reloading the copied URL, keyboard, drag, reduced motion, paging to the left on a surface without chapters, and live arrival from a real Haiku run. Record screenshots and the result as evidence per requirement; send any failure, including any visual difference from the mock, back to the build task.

acceptance_criteria: ac-one-event: Given the built dashboard is open on the chat screen with an agent's output panel expanded, against a Hub whose stream the drive controls, when the Hub emits exactly one context_warning event for that agent, then the tab's network log shows at most one GET for each route it re-reads, and no GET of /agents/{name}/output

ac-no-overlap: Given the dashboard is open against a Hub that delays GET /agents by 2s, when five events that affect the agent list arrive within 500ms, then the network log never shows two GET /agents in flight at once, and shows no more than two GET /agents in total

ac-line-appears: Given a conversation is open with its history loaded, when the Hub streams one agent output line for that conversation, then the line is visible in the conversation, and the network log shows no GET of that conversation's chat history, no GET of /agents/{name}/output and no GET /agents

ac-run-budget-claude: Given a scratch Hub runs on a copy of the trial database, and a real Claude (Haiku) turn is streaming on the open conversation, when the turn streams for at least two minutes, then no one-minute window of the tab's network log holds more than 40 requests to the Hub

ac-run-budget-copilot: Given a scratch Hub runs on a copy of the trial database, and a real Copilot turn is streaming on the open conversation, when the turn streams for at least two minutes, then no one-minute window of the tab's network log holds more than 40 requests to the Hub

ac-run-budget-codex: Given a scratch Hub replays a recorded Codex turn's event stream onto the open conversation at its recorded pace (live Codex once the operator's account exists), when the replay streams for at least two minutes, then no one-minute window of the tab's network log holds more than 40 requests to the Hub
ac-idle-budget: Given the dashboard is open on the chat screen with nothing running, when five minutes pass with no operator input, then the tab sends no more than 30 requests to the Hub in total
ac-lists-now: Given a copy of the operator's database, when each of the three routes is requested five times in turn, then each route's median answer time is under 60ms

ac-lists-10x: Given a copy with agent_outputs, event_logs and trace_spans each multiplied ten times, when each of the three routes is requested five times in turn, then each route's median is under 1.5 times its median on the original copy

ac-loops: Given a copy of the operator's database with a statement counter on the engine, when GET /loops and GET /jobs are each requested five times, then each request issues no more than 25 statements, and each route's median answer time is under 80ms

ac-same: Given a copy of the operator's database, and the master revision this slice starts from, when each listed route is requested on both revisions against the same copy, then the response bodies are equal, apart from fields that state the current time

ac-streams: Given a Hub on a scratch database, when 50 project event streams are opened and held, then one more is opened and GET /agents is requested, then the 51st stream receives its first frame, and GET /agents answers 200 in under 1 second
ac-burst: Given a copy of the operator's database served in process with the lifespan off, when 24 concurrent requests of the poll mix are sent at once, then every one answers within 600ms

tasks.description:
Write the slice's acceptance drive as scripts/drive/perf_responsive.py, with one `--scenario` per criterion: one-event, no-overlap, line-appears, run-budget (`--runner claude|copilot|codex-replay|codex`), idle-budget, lists, lists-10x, loops, same-answers (`--base <sha>`), streams and burst. Each scenario prints its measurement and exits non-zero on failure. Run every scenario on master and record the baseline numbers in the task notes.

The in-process scenarios run against copies of a database (`--db`) with the Hub lifespan off.

The browser scenarios use a scratch Hub on a trial-database copy and a headless page with a request log.

The drive must never contact :8000 or write the operator's database. It must refuse to start a Hub on a copy with the lifespan on unless jobs, loops and queued input in that copy are disabled first, because doing so spawned a real agent run during the investigation.

requirement_links.latest_rejection_reason:
REVISION NEEDED. The streaming work is good and meets every acceptance criterion when driven. But turning the questions and permission-request polls into failure-only backstops introduces a regression. Two kinds of state change that only the 3s poll ever showed are now never refetched.

WHAT I DROVE at 3ca9314 (scripts/drive/perf_responsive.py on a copy of the trial DB, all PASS):
- line-appears: the line is visible, with no GETs after it and no forbidden GETs.
- idle-budget: 0 requests in 300s.
- run-budget, claude haiku: busiest one-minute window 31 (limit 40).
- run-budget, copilot: busiest window 33.
- run-budget, codex-replay: busiest window 0.
Also ran: vitest on streamedLineWithoutRefetch and useSSE-handle-once (9 passed); tsc and eslint clean. I read the history route (agent_chat.py:655-806) against insertStreamedOutput. Its ordering (time-sorted delivered, queued appended last) is matched, and the runs map is still refreshed by the queue and run-terminal events.

DEFECT 1, the one sending this back: an expired permission request stays on screen as pending.
- Some code paths set a PermissionRequest to 'expired' without broadcasting anything:
  - expire_pending_for_run (permission_requests.py:20-36), called at run end from agent_trigger.py:2954/3284/3624/4572/4674 and run_reconciliation.py:88;
  - the Copilot permission timeout (agent_trigger.py:3994-3999).
- Before this change, the 3000ms refetchInterval on usePendingPermissionRequests picked these up within 3s.
- Now backstopAfterFailure polls only after a failed read. Nothing else covers it:
  - the run_* cases in useSSE.ts:559-580 do not invalidate ['project',pid,'permission-requests'];
  - refetchOnWindowFocus is false (main.tsx:17).
- Result: when a run ends with a request unanswered, AgentOutputPanel keeps showing a live Allow/Deny card instead of the expired, dismissable one. Clicking Allow/Deny returns 409, because decide refuses non-pending requests (permissions.py:144-146). It stays that way until a reload or an unrelated permission event.
- The backstopPoll.ts comment says "a dropped event is healed by reconnect". These are not dropped events: no event is ever sent.

DEFECT 2, same class: questions' asker_waiting.
- list_questions computes asker_waiting from run status (questions.py:443-457).
- A run ending changes it with no question_* event, so the question card keeps saying the agent is waiting after its run ended.

SUGGESTED FIX: on run_completed, run_failed, run_stopped and run_interrupted, invalidate ['project',pid,'permission-requests'] and ['project',pid,'questions'] in applyInvalidation. That is one refetch per run end, not per line, so the budget is unaffected. Alternatively, broadcast permission_decided from the expiry paths. Either way, add a unit test that fails today: render the panel with a pending request, push run_completed, and expect the list to be refetched.

MINOR, verify while there: useAgentChatHistory applies a line whose conversation_id is null to whichever conversation is open (agentChat.ts:407 only skips a non-null mismatch). The history route filters on conversation_id equality, so it would never return that line. If record_output can receive conversation_id=None, skip such lines rather than insert them.

EVIDENCE: ev-6f184b5f8b6a (FR-3) holds on its own terms; the line-appears drive confirms it. ev-f23a30b0ea7a (FR-4) holds for the budgets: all four drives pass, measured above. Both are rejected with this verdict only because the commit ships the defect above. Re-record them on the fixed commit and quote the drive numbers.

No side findings filed.

REVISION NEEDED. The streaming work is good and meets every acceptance criterion when driven. But turning the questions and permission-request polls into failure-only backstops introduces a regression. Two kinds of state change that only the 3s poll ever showed are now never refetched.

WHAT I DROVE at 3ca9314 (scripts/drive/perf_responsive.py on a copy of the trial DB, all PASS):
- line-appears: the line is visible, with no GETs after it and no forbidden GETs.
- idle-budget: 0 requests in 300s.
- run-budget, claude haiku: busiest one-minute window 31 (limit 40).
- run-budget, copilot: busiest window 33.
- run-budget, codex-replay: busiest window 0.
Also ran: vitest on streamedLineWithoutRefetch and useSSE-handle-once (9 passed); tsc and eslint clean. I read the history route (agent_chat.py:655-806) against insertStreamedOutput. Its ordering (time-sorted delivered, queued appended last) is matched, and the runs map is still refreshed by the queue and run-terminal events.

DEFECT 1, the one sending this back: an expired permission request stays on screen as pending.
- Some code paths set a PermissionRequest to 'expired' without broadcasting anything:
  - expire_pending_for_run (permission_requests.py:20-36), called at run end from agent_trigger.py:2954/3284/3624/4572/4674 and run_reconciliation.py:88;
  - the Copilot permission timeout (agent_trigger.py:3994-3999).
- Before this change, the 3000ms refetchInterval on usePendingPermissionRequests picked these up within 3s.
- Now backstopAfterFailure polls only after a failed read. Nothing else covers it:
  - the run_* cases in useSSE.ts:559-580 do not invalidate ['project',pid,'permission-requests'];
  - refetchOnWindowFocus is false (main.tsx:17).
- Result: when a run ends with a request unanswered, AgentOutputPanel keeps showing a live Allow/Deny card instead of the expired, dismissable one. Clicking Allow/Deny returns 409, because decide refuses non-pending requests (permissions.py:144-146). It stays that way until a reload or an unrelated permission event.
- The backstopPoll.ts comment says "a dropped event is healed by reconnect". These are not dropped events: no event is ever sent.

DEFECT 2, same class: questions' asker_waiting.
- list_questions computes asker_waiting from run status (questions.py:443-457).
- A run ending changes it with no question_* event, so the question card keeps saying the agent is waiting after its run ended.

SUGGESTED FIX: on run_completed, run_failed, run_stopped and run_interrupted, invalidate ['project',pid,'permission-requests'] and ['project',pid,'questions'] in applyInvalidation. That is one refetch per run end, not per line, so the budget is unaffected. Alternatively, broadcast permission_decided from the expiry paths. Either way, add a unit test that fails today: render the panel with a pending request, push run_completed, and expect the list to be refetched.

MINOR, verify while there: useAgentChatHistory applies a line whose conversation_id is null to whichever conversation is open (agentChat.ts:407 only skips a non-null mismatch). The history route filters on conversation_id equality, so it would never return that line. If record_output can receive conversation_id=None, skip such lines rather than insert them.

EVIDENCE: ev-6f184b5f8b6a (FR-3) holds on its own terms; the line-appears drive confirms it. ev-f23a30b0ea7a (FR-4) holds for the budgets: all four drives pass, measured above. Both are rejected with this verdict only because the commit ships the defect above. Re-record them on the fixed commit and quote the drive numbers.

No side findings filed.

The operator asked (2026-10-26) for a mock of a redesigned Spec tab AND the conversation's spec side panel: better buttons, prettier, more animation, fitting AgentWeave's aesthetic like the rest of the app's overhaul, plus better navigation, filtering and ordering. Read the document first: read_spec_document('spec/changes/the-spec-page-redesigned/spec.json', include='full'). It is still exploring; this task is the 'mock' task in it. Context for the actions shown: roadmap spec/changes/flows-that-do-not-stall-after-the-october-25-retrospective/spec.json (slices C 'Check, approve and build are separate' and D 'A build has a driver, a level and its people').

Follow hub/ui/mock/README.md exactly: presentational components in hub/ui/src/components/spec/ (props in, callbacks out, no fetching), CSS in hub/ui/src/styles/, tokens and primitives only, data-slot on every button, words are the operator's, motion tokens + reduced motion, mock state marked `// mock state`. Replace/extend mock/screens/Spec.tsx and the conversation screen's spec panel. Do NOT touch hub/hub/static/ui (the :8000 bundle). Brand kit: brand/ (tokens.json, identity-record.md); the LoadingThread motif is the app's loading language.

Design direction (a starting point, not a cage; improve on it):
1. Header: breadcrumb (roadmap > slice), title, phase pill, a journey ribbon (writing -> approved -> building -> done) that animates between states, and the actions as real buttons: Check (ghost, never changes phase, shows a '2 blocking - 1 warning' result pill), Approve (primary when ready), Build / 'Approve and build' (split button). Only the actions open to the state show; one is primary.
2. Document rendered natively from the document structure (no SpecFrame): summary/problem, requirement cards (FR id, modal, statement, collapsible criteria, evidence-state chip, linked task chips), tasks (list, or build order with dependency lines). Check results appear inline beside what they concern and as markers in the outline.
3. Navigation: an outline rail (sections, requirements with evidence dots, tasks) that jumps and highlights; previous/next slice and roadmap links; back/forward; copy-link on every position.
4. Document list: search, filter chips (kind, phase, 'building now'), order menu (last change, phase, title, roadmap order), slices grouped under their roadmap in build order, a live pulse on documents with a build running; the choice persists.
5. Within-document filter bar: requirements by evidence state and by task; tasks by status and agent; order tasks by status or build order.
6. Builds section: one card per build: driver (Hub flow / lead agent / by hand), level badge (Fast / Reviewed / Gated), people, a task-status bar, a stacked time bar (building / waiting for review / checks / waiting to be handed out), cost split build/review/lead, runs; a running build animates and advances as mock state. A 'Start a build' dialog: driver segmented, level segmented with one line on what each means, builders, reviewers (several), lead, budget cap, window, lands on (main or a branch). Mock only.
7. Side panel: the same components in one column; outline becomes a menu; tabs Document / Tasks / Builds; nothing clipped at its narrowest width.
8. The document's open question 2: give the mock bar a toggle between 'document list as a left column' and 'top switcher, document full width' so the operator can compare.

Deliver: the mock running (npx vite --config vite.mock.config.ts), `npx tsc -p tsconfig.mock.json --noEmit` and `npm run lint` clean, and screenshots via mock/shoot.py into testbed/ui-judge/mock/spec in dark, light and narrow, including the side panel. Note: node_modules may not be linked into your worktree; install inside it if needed. When done, complete the task with notes naming the screenshots and send a short message to Architect; Architect reviews, and the operator approves the look.

requirement_links.statement: A document's header shows its phase and the actions open to it as buttons: Check while it is being written (never changing its phase), Approve when it is ready, Build or 'Approve and build' once it may be built, with the one the document is waiting for visually primary.
Pressing Check shows what blocks approval and what only warns, beside the parts of the document they concern, without leaving the page or freezing the document.
The document's sections, requirements, acceptance criteria and tasks are rendered by the app from the document's structure, so the page can filter, order, highlight and link them.

The document list can be filtered by kind, phase, text and 'has a build running', ordered by last change, phase, title or roadmap order, and grouped under its roadmap, and the choice persists per project.
Within a document, requirements can be filtered by evidence state and by task, and tasks by status and agent; tasks can be ordered by status or by build order (dependencies).

An outline of the open document jumps to any section, requirement or task; a slice links to its roadmap and to the previous and next slice; back and forward return to the previous position; every position has a link that reopens it.

Each build of the document shows, live: its driver, level and people; tasks by status; wall time split into building, waiting for review, checks and waiting to be handed out; runs; and cost split between building, reviewing and leading.
The conversation's spec side panel shows the same document, actions, navigation and build progress as the Spec tab, in a layout that fits the panel's width.

The page uses only the app's tokens and primitives, works in dark and light, animates state changes (opening, checking, a build's progress) with the motion tokens, and stops animating under reduced motion.
A mock of the Spec tab and the side panel, built from the real components fed recorded fixtures under hub/ui/mock, is approved by the operator before the page is wired to the Hub.

The side panel switches to any other document from a switcher above its tabs; jumps to any section, and to any requirement or task from a strip that shows each one's state, with previous and next and its position; and filters and orders from one tray whose active choices stay visible as chips that remove themselves one at a time or all at once.

Choosing a spec to open, from the panel's Specs tab, the Ctrl/Cmd+K picker or the panel's switcher, is one picker: a search field from which Enter opens the first match it names; with nothing typed, shortcuts to the conversation's attached document, to documents with a build running (with their progress) and to the last three opened; then every document with the Spec tab's filters, order and roadmap grouping. Opening never attaches a document to the conversation.

reviewer-takes-it: Given a task created by create_task outside any flow, completed by DeveloperOpus and still held by it, when QA calls update_task(status='under_review'), then the move succeeds, QA is the holder, and QA can then approve or send it back; fails on master 43301a6 with 403
author-refused: Given the same completed task, when DeveloperOpus calls update_task(status='under_review') or (status='approved'), then both are refused, as today
mender-author-refused: Given a task whose evidence the mender re-recorded, when the mender tries to move it to under_review or approved, then both are refused

same-answer: Given a completed task held by its author, and the same task held by a reviewer, when the same move is attempted by the same actor through update_task, the flow's review claim and the mender's reset, then each path gives the same verdict and the same refusal reason; a test asserts this for every status, holder and actor the invariant test enumerates

tasks.description: Resolve spdoc- ids in list_evidence and record_evidence as read_spec_document does; test both, red first.
tasks.notes:
Approved; this accepts ev-acca7e187df5 (FR-7 at 918bc5e4f4ee).

What I checked:
- Diff against c2eabc3: a new `_find_document` in hub/hub/api/v1/agent_actions.py resolves `spdoc-…` with the same `_DOCUMENT_ID_RE` and the same project-scoped id lookup that read_spec_document uses. It falls back to `spec_lifecycle.get_document` for a path. It is used both in `_resolve_requirement` (record_evidence) and in `list_evidence_for_agent`. Because the lookup is limited to the caller's project, another project's id still answers 404.
- Red first: I put c2eabc3's agent_actions.py back in place and ran hub/tests/test_evidence_tools_accept_document_ids.py. It failed with `assert 404 == 201`, because the record by spdoc id was refused. With the change it passes. I restored the file afterwards and the tree is clean.
- The test drives the HTTP routes end to end. It records evidence by spdoc id (201), then lists by id, by path, and by id plus FR-1. All three answer 200 with identical bodies, one row each. That matches the spdoc-id-works criterion.
- ruff and black (py311) are clean on both files. I ran 339 related tests (every *evidence* test, agent_actions_*, spec_read*, the land-gate test and the reviewer-does-not-record test): all passed.
- I did not drive it against a live Hub, because the running Hub serves master, not this branch. The route-level test stands in for that check.
No side findings filed.

requirement_links.latest_rejection_reason:
The behaviour is right, but the change breaks CI lint, so it goes back.

**Blocking: `ruff check hub/` fails with 2 F401 errors that this change introduced.** At hub/hub/api/v1/agent_actions.py:1568 (`from ... import spec_index, spec_lifecycle` in `_resolve_requirement`) and :1700 (`from ... import spec_lifecycle` in `list_evidence_for_agent`), `spec_lifecycle` is now unused because both call sites moved to `_find_document`. On the parent commit (c2eabc3) ruff over this file is clean, and these 2 errors are the only ruff failures in all of `hub/`. To fix: drop the two unused imports (`ruff check --fix` handles it).

**Nit, not blocking:** `_find_document` writes the regex inline as `r"spdoc-[0-9a-f]+"` when `_DOCUMENT_ID_RE` already exists in the same module (line 1869) for `read_spec_document`. Using it would keep the two in step, since "as read_spec_document does" is the requirement.

**What I checked:**
- New test test_evidence_tools_accept_document_ids.py passes on 0de0b5e. With the parent's agent_actions.py it fails, with `record_evidence` by spdoc id returning 404, so the red-first check holds.
- The test covers the criterion `spdoc-id-works`: record by id returns 201, list by id equals list by path, and the identifier filter works.
- Evidence/spec_document/agent_actions subset of hub/tests: 490 passed, 2 skipped.
- black --check passes.
- The MCP layer passes `document` straight through, so the tools reach the fixed route.

Evidence ev-8abd997482a2 (FR-7) is rejected with this verdict because of the lint failure only. Its claim itself is substantiated. No side findings filed.

tasks.notes:
Approved. What I checked at 6a0a939, against FR-5 close-in-one-step and FR-6 evidence-awaits-review as their how_to_check states them:
- I ran tests/test_close_spec_tasks_already_built.py together with test_migrations.py and test_project_persistence.py: 165 passed, 1 skipped. The close test approves a four-task chained document in a real git repo, closes it against a commit on main, and checks that all four are under_review and held by nobody, and that the run count does not change (FR-5). The evidence test checks four awaiting pieces whose locator and footprint name the commit. It accepts three, out of dependency order, through QA's agent route and rejects one. Three tasks end approved and delta stays under_review. Every history row names "already built" and the short sha, and the last row says "accepted by QA" (FR-6). The operator's own acceptance route also approves. A commit not on main gets 422 and changes nothing, and a document that is not approved gets 409.
- Regression check over the shared seams it touched (requirement_evidence.record awaiting=, apply_transition note=/closing_with=, both decide routes): requirement_evidence, task_transition_service, task_transitions, the transitions API, approval_refuses_unaccepted_evidence, agent_evidence_plane, the reviewer's verdict decides the task's evidence, operator evidence names its commit, decision announced, duplicate evidence, agent evidence grant. 240 passed.
- ruff on the changed Python is clean. black --check over hub/hub and hub/tests is clean. UI: closeAlreadyBuilt.test.tsx passed 4/4 under vitest, and tsc --noEmit and eslint on the changed files are clean.
- Migration 0147 is one additive nullable column (task_transitions.note). Master has no competing 0147 as of 8fe0b3f, and it follows the round-trip pattern in test_migrations. I accept going outside the declared file list here, because FR-6 needs the history to name the action and the commit.
- Not driven live: trial Hub :8010 runs master, so the route is not served there. The ASGI-over-real-git route tests are the criteria's stated how_to_check.
Evidence: I accept ev-a6c3640f5e92 (FR-5) and ev-572b2c3a1bec (FR-6) on the runs above. No side findings filed. The author's note to whoever lands next still stands: expect a UI-bundle conflict with landing-explains-itself, and rebuild the bundle rather than hand-merging it.

acceptance_criteria: board-review-picker: Given a completed task held by its author, DeveloperOpus, in the operator's app, when the operator opens the task's status menu and moves it into review, then the app asks which agent reviews it, lists every open agent except DeveloperOpus, and after choosing QA the task is under_review held by QA; at no point is 'Move to Under review' offered as a move that keeps DeveloperOpus as holder

menu-offers-only-allowed: Given each status and holder the invariant test enumerates, when the board's status menu is rendered for the operator, then every move it offers is one the mover decision allows the operator, and a test asserts the menu's moves equal the decision's answer

late-requirement-merges: Given a task linked to FR-1..FR-10 of its document, whose document then gains FR-11, and evidence for FR-11 recorded on that task from its checkout at a later commit and accepted, when the operator lands the task, then the later commit merges with it, and the task's requirement links include FR-11; on master 43301a6 the landing is refused as 'commits on neither master nor inside any commit the accepted evidence names'

awaiting-evidence-offered: Given a completed task whose branch tip is named only by evidence still awaiting a decision, when the operator presses Land, then the refusal names that evidence by requirement and commit and shows Accept and Reject beside it; accepting it there and pressing Land again lands the task

running-checks-wait: Given a completed task whose checks are running on the commit approval would merge, when the operator presses Land, then the app says the landing waits for the checks and offers no 'Land anyway'; 'Land anyway' with a reason is offered only once a check has failed

wait-shows-progress: Given a completed task whose checks have been running for 8 minutes and whose previous check run took 14 minutes, when the operator opens the task, then beside Land, without scrolling, it reads that it waits for checks running 8 minutes of about 14; when the run passes, Land becomes available without a reload and the operator receives a notification naming the task

disabled-looks-disabled: Given the 'Land anyway' control with no reason typed, when it is rendered, then it is visibly disabled and its title says a reason is needed; pressing it does nothing and says nothing new
tasks.description: Evidence recorded on a task against its own document's requirement counts toward its merge (link on record, or count it in the merge-target query; the builder picks and says why), red test first from the 2026-10-26 sequence. Refusals of approve/land name each cause with its remedy (awaiting evidence with Accept/Reject in place, a missing link, running checks as a wait with no override). The board's status menu offers only allowed moves and a review hand-off asks for the reviewer. The drawer shows the checks' wait beside Land with elapsed and previous duration, notifies on finish, and disabled controls look disabled. Rebuild the UI bundle.
tasks.notes:
Approved at 218e879 (second round; the prior blocker, test_surface_ceilings, is fixed: 6/6 pass).

What I ran in the review checkout:
- Backend: py -3.11 -m pytest test_landing_explains_itself, test_every_task_state_has_a_mover, test_surface_ceilings, test_ui_build_stamp, test_task_integration, test_requirement_gate*, test_project_checks* → 200 passed, 1 skipped. ruff and black (py311) are clean on all 6 changed Python files.
- Red-first check for FR-10: I swapped in the base (a4c461a) requirement_evidence.py and ran test_evidence_for_a_requirement_the_document_gained_merges_with_the_task. It fails: on base the approval left the later commit off main. It passes with the fix. I restored the file and the checkout is clean.
- UI: vitest landingExplainsItself, taskStatusControl and taskLandingAction → 36 passed. The full vitest suite → 2370 passed across 233 files. tsc --noEmit and eslint on the changed files are clean. The bundle-stamp test passes.
- Drive: I started a scratch Hub from this branch on :8021 with a throwaway DB (not :8010, which runs the flow). For a completed task, GET /moves answered moves [rejected, revision_needed, under_review] with a reviewers list, and PATCH {status: under_review, assignee: QA} → under_review held by QA. The author-excluded case was not reproduced on the scratch Hub, because a bare run row is not an authorship source. It is covered by the route tests, which pass: they exclude the author from reviewers and refuse a keep-the-author PATCH with 403. I did not do the Playwright/screenshot steps. My first approve was itself refused with 'checks are still running … can be retried when they finish', which is the wait behaving as designed.

Evidence, per requirement:
- FR-9 (ev-06c529b27631): _reviewers_for builds the list from decide_move itself, and a test asserts the moves equal the decision for every enumerated (status, holder). The drawer replaces 'Move to Under review' with 'Hand to a reviewer…', which opens a picker over route.reviewers.
- FR-10 (ev-624ef644475e): recording evidence links a requirement of the task's own document. I chose this over widening _targets, because it keeps one rule for what a task serves. The test is green and red on base.
- FR-11 (ev-7aa9439f115e): the refusal now carries unlinked entries with the link as remedy. The Hub's hub-tests check for task-8618731d065d (2026-10-27) failed on one test, and the same test fails on main too:

`hub/tests/test_turn_starts_never_freeze_the_hub.py::test_a_turn_start_that_creates_its_checkout_never_stalls_the_loop`

The full run gave 1 failed, 9071 passed. Run on its own, the file passes (3 passed in 9s, QA at 885e6cc). So the test is timing-dependent: it fails under the load of the full suite and of a busy machine. During that window the Hub was also returning "database is busy" 503s.

Because the check fails on main, it blocks every approval from merging without an operator override. Make the test deterministic, or fix the stall it detects if that stall is real.
tasks.notes:
QA2 review at 09617d3: approved. The change is test-only: the task_turn fixture now awaits await_background_runs() after the warm start (hub/tests/test_turn_starts_never_freeze_the_hub.py:128). No assertion changed and no product code changed.

What I ran:
- The root cause holds. The stub _spawn runs as a task in agent_trigger._background_runs (agent_trigger.py:2115) and sets Run.status=completed only after several awaits. The measured turn's check for a running run (agent_trigger.py:1190-1194) can therefore see the warm run still 'running'.
- I reproduced it deterministically by injecting `await asyncio.sleep(0.2)` into _spawn. With the fix removed: 1 failed, 2 passed, raising exactly `TriggerAgentError: writer already has a run in progress.` With the fix: 3 passed. The injection was reverted afterwards.
- The file as committed passed 3 times in a row (3 passed each run, about 10 s).
- ruff check and black --check are clean on the file.
- I did not run the full suite. The diff is five lines in one test fixture, and the deterministic repro covers the load-dependent path.
- It is not a real product stall. Refusing a second concurrent run for the same agent is correct behaviour.

Evidence ev-221d7b47583e is accepted for what it claims: the command and output reproduce as stated, and its covers=partial is honest. It says itself that it is not evidence for FR-1's statement. It is linked to FR-1 only because this task lives in that document. Accepting it must not be read as FR-1 coverage. FR-1's real evidence is on the task-movers task.

No side findings filed.

requirement_links.statement: Every question the Hub's mender asks through `ask_user` is recorded with `blocking` false and no `wait_expires_at`, whatever `blocking` value it passed; the call returns without waiting; it parks no task; and a blocking question from any other agent still waits as today.

requirement_links.statement: Each of a project's checks has a 'fast' setting that the operator sets in the app's project settings and through the project settings route. It defaults to off for every check saved before or without it. A check marked fast with a timeout over 120 seconds is refused with a reason naming the limit. A task's check run executes its fast checks before its other checks.

When an agent moves its task to completed and the project has fast checks that apply to the work, the Hub first commits the agent's uncommitted work in the task's checkout to the task branch. It then runs the fast checks on the commit the task's review would be given, merged onto the main branch, before the completion is recorded.

When a fast check fails with a failure of the task's own, the completion is refused (409) and the task stays in_progress, held by its builder. The message the agent's update_task tool returns names each failing check, the commit checked and the check run, and quotes the check's output (its failure excerpt or the last 4000 characters).

An agent's completion waits at most 120 seconds for the fast checks. When they have not decided within that time, the completion is recorded and the checks continue as part of the task's check run. A failure they find later returns the task to its builder like any other.

The fast checks run at completion are the start of the task's check run for that work. The remaining checks continue in the same run, and no fast check is executed a second time for the same merged tree.

The update_task tool's description says that moving a task to completed runs the project's fast checks on the committed work, can take up to two minutes, and is refused with their output when one fails.

requirement_links.statement: A flow queues no review of a completed task while the task's check run for the work under review is running, has not started, or was superseded. The firing records the task as deferred, saying how long its checks have run and how long the previous run took. While that is all the flow is waiting on, the firing is not recorded as stalled and no loop_stalled stall is raised.

When a task's check run ends failed with a failure of the task's own while the task is completed, the Hub moves the task to revision_needed, held by the agent that built it, and queues and starts no review of that work. The task's notes carry the failing checks, the commit and their output. The transition is recorded with origin 'checks' and a note naming the run, and the app's history attributes it to the project's checks, not to the operator.
When a completed flow task's check run passes, or ends with no failure of the task's own, the flow queues the task's review within 60 seconds, without waiting for its next scheduled tick.

Outside a flow, completion is gated and a failed task is returned as inside one. An agent cannot move a completed task to under_review, and the mender cannot hand it to a reviewer, while its check run is undecided or has failed with the task's own failure; the refusal states the run's state and how long it has run. The operator's own review dispatch is not refused.

requirement_links.statement: A reviewer sending a task back can name the pieces of evidence that fail, each with its own reason, in the same action that sends it back; only the named pieces become rejected, each with its own reason.
On a send-back, every awaiting piece of the task that the reviewer did not name as failing becomes held at its commit: not rejected, not accepted, and shown as held with the send-back's reason.
A send-back that names no failing piece is allowed when it gives a reason (a defect outside any requirement, a failing check), and then every awaiting piece is held.
A held piece never counts as accepted evidence; the requirement it served needs a new piece at the builder's next commit, and the reviewer's next verdict judges that new piece.
Neither the reviewer nor anyone else needs a separate evidence decision before or after the verdict: the send-back or approval decides every awaiting piece of the task in the one action.
Approving a task while naming any of its pieces as failing is refused, naming the contradiction.

list_evidence, the task's history and the app's evidence views show each piece's outcome (accepted, rejected, held, awaiting) with its own reason and who decided it, and filtering by review state distinguishes held from rejected.
The review turn's brief and the update_task tool's description tell the reviewer how to name failing pieces and that unnamed ones are held, not rejected.

requirement_links.statement: A check's failure counts as main's only when every pytest node id that failed on the task's merged commit (after its serial rerun) also fails when exactly those ids are run with the same serial command on main at the commit the check run was cut from; a failing id that passes there is the task's own and the task goes back to its builder; exit codes and failure counts are never compared.

Before a failure is charged to anyone, the failed node ids are run once more on the same tree and nothing else, serially (the command's xdist worker count set to 0 and its distribution options dropped); if they all pass the failure is a flake and the check passes, recorded as flaky with the ids; if any fails again it stands and is compared with main.

When every failure in the task's check run for the work approval would merge is main's or a flake, and the project's automatic override is on, an approval by an actor the mover rules otherwise permit (a reviewer's run or the operator) lands the task with no reason typed; the approval transition records override_by 'hub' and an override_reason naming each check and test id, whether it fails on main or passed on its own, the check run id, the main commit sha, and the fix task; the transition's actor stays the approver.

An override is never automatic for: a failing id that passes on main; a failing or flaky test whose file is among the paths the task's merged work changes against the run's main commit; on a Hub-filed fix task, the ids it was filed for; a check whose failures pytest did not name in full (a non-pytest check, a timeout, a truncated summary, more than 50 failures, a command that cannot be narrowed); or a run with no main answer. Each keeps today's answer: sent back to its builder, or held for the operator where the whole check fails on main too.

Each project has a setting, on by default for new and existing projects and shown with the project's checks in the app's settings, that turns off both the automatic override and the fix-task filing; off, approval over main's failures or flakes behaves exactly as before this change (held for the operator, who lands it with a typed reason).

A reviewer briefed on a task whose failing checks are all main's or flakes is told they are not the task's work, that approving lands it with an override the Hub records, and which fix task covers them; it is not told to send the task back.

requirement_links.statement: A turn resumes the conversation's provider session only when that session is recorded as created by the CLI of the agent's bound runner. When it is recorded as another CLI's, the turn starts a new session: a Claude launch carries no --resume, a Codex exec launch no 'resume <id>', and a Copilot turn is given no session to load.

On a turn that starts a new session because the session was another CLI's, the conversation gives up that session before the run starts, so the session the new CLI creates becomes the conversation's without a binding conflict, and the next turn on the same CLI resumes it.

A turn resumes the conversation's session as today when the agent was rebound to another runner of the same CLI (for example a Claude runner with another model) or to the same runner, and when the session's CLI is unknown (not backfilled, typed by the operator, a job's stored id, or self-reported).

A turn that starts a new session because the agent now runs on another CLI records one info diagnostic (code runner.session_not_carried) in the conversation, before anything the runner emits, and prepends the same sentence to the agent's prompt. The sentence names the agent, the CLI the earlier turns ran on and the CLI it runs on now, and says the earlier turns are not in the new session. A turn that resumes records none.

On a runner with no model provider, a model stored on the conversation is applied only when the bound runner's CLI declares it (by id or alias) or when no CLI in the model catalog declares it. Otherwise the turn launches with the runner's own model, and the stored model stays on the conversation, so a turn after rebinding back to its CLI applies it again.

A turn that starts a new session while a stored model is withheld records one info diagnostic (code runner.model_withheld) naming the stored model, the CLI that does not offer it and the model the turn runs on. Resumed turns of that session do not repeat it.

A turn's run_started event, and the timeline's 'Run started (runner, model)' line, name the model the CLI was launched with, and its turn_usage row names the model the CLI reported. After a rebind to another CLI, neither names a model that only the previous CLI declares.

In one conversation, a Claude agent rebound to a Copilot runner and then back to Claude runs one turn on each binding, each completing on its first delivery: no run fails, no queue entry is redelivered, and each turn's recorded model is one its own CLI ran.

The migration records, for each existing conversation that holds a provider session, the runner recorded on that conversation's latest completed run that bound the same session id. It leaves the CLI unknown when there is no such run. Its downgrade removes the column and changes nothing else.

requirement_links.statement: In a project with checks configured, a move to approved that is refused for no other reason is recorded at once and queues the task's work for landing. It is not refused because the task's check result is missing, still running, or was produced on an earlier main tip. Approving starts no per-task check run. Approval is still refused when the task's own confirmed check failure is recorded for the same merge targets.

Tasks queued for landing in one project are landed together in a batch. Main's tip, with every batch task's merge targets merged in queue order, gets one run of the project's checks. When that run passes, every task in the batch reaches main and no further check run is started for any of them.

After a batch lands, the tree at main's tip equals the tree the batch's checks passed on, and each landed task has one merged integration record per merge target, with the commits that rode along. If main's tip moved after the batch was built, nothing lands from the stale batch, and the batch is built and checked again on the new tip.

No approval, landing, integration retry, mend resolution or checkout release holds a database write transaction open while a git command or a check runs. A write from another database connection made while that git runs completes without waiting for it.

Every merge the Hub makes into main goes through the landing queue, at most one batch at a time per project. That covers approval, retrying an integration, landing a mend resolution, and integrating approved work whose evidence was accepted afterwards. With no checks configured, the landing still runs after the approval commits, and the request that caused it answers with the integration outcome as it does today. With checks configured, the request answers at once with the task queued.

If the Hub stops while a batch is being checked or landed, then after it starts again no queued task is lost and none is merged twice. A batch left checking is recorded interrupted and its tasks are queued again in their original order. A batch that had already moved main is recorded landed from what main contains.

requirement_links.statement: When a batch's checks fail with a confirmed failure that is not main's, the Hub finds the first task in queue order whose work, added to the tasks before it, makes the failing tests fail. Only that task goes back to its author (approved to revision_needed), with the failing output and the tasks it was landed on. The rest of the batch is checked again as the next batch and lands if it passes. Finding the task takes at most ceil(log2(n)) narrowed runs for a batch of n, and each narrowed run executes only the failed tests when the check is a plain pytest command.

A queued task whose work does not merge cleanly onto main plus the batch tasks before it is taken out of the batch before any check runs. It is sent back to its author naming the conflicting paths and the tasks it conflicts with, and the rest of the batch proceeds without it.

A queued task lands only in a batch where every task whose commit its merge targets contain has already landed or comes earlier in the same batch. If such a prerequisite is sent back, the dependent stays queued, is not sent back, and its landing names the prerequisite it waits for.

When every confirmed failure in a batch's run also fails on the main tip the batch was built on, the batch is not narrowed. It follows slice M's rule: with M's automatic override on, the batch lands with the override recorded on the batch and on each task's integration record, and one fix task is filed per failing check, not one per task. With the override off, the batch waits for the operator, who can land it with one reason. A failure that passes when re-run on the same tree counts as a pass, and the flaky test is recorded.

Each run is counted in exactly one role: mending (a run of the Hub's mender), leading (a run slice D records as a build's lead), reviewing (a run that took a review turn of a task, or a run bound to a completed or under_review task by an agent other than the one recorded completing it), building (any other run bound to a task), or other (none of these); cost, run time and run count are shown per role, the mender's on a line of its own.

A mender run counts toward the spec document whose task or flow the stall it was woken for names (the stall's task's document, or its loop's document), and toward 'not from a spec' only when the stall names neither.

Each build's wall time, from its first task leaving pending to its last task's approval (or now, while it runs), is split into building, reviewing, checks, held by a failed check, waiting for review and waiting to be handed out, by the precedence in the 'wall-time partition' algorithm, and the parts sum to the wall time to the second.
Check runs are shown on their own line per spec, per build and per level: how many ran, how many passed and failed, and their total running time, apart from any agent's run time.

A send-back (a task moved from under_review to revision_needed or rejected) counts once, attributed to the agent, model and level of the run recorded as completing the work that was sent back, and to the reviewer agent and model that sent it back.

Evidence verdicts are counted per piece by its own outcome (accepted, rejected, held, awaiting), attributed to the model and agent of the run that recorded the piece; a send-back that names one failing piece among four counts one rejected and three held.

The view counts, per spec, reviewer agent and reviewer model, the send-backs made by a review run while the task's newest check run that started before the review ended had failed, with those reviews' cost and run time.

The project view shows the same figures grouped by spec, by agent, by model and by level, each grouping with a totals row equal to the others' and a 'since' date applied to all of them; work with no build recorded appears under its spec as 'before builds' and under level as 'no level recorded'.

A run with no priced cost is counted as unpriced and shown as a count beside the cost, never added as $0; Copilot credits are summed in their own unit; a figure no row reports is shown as unknown, not 0.

prerequisites.title: The acceptance drive, the baselines and the candidate

requirement_links.statement: Both builds start from the same main commit and use the same driver (the Hub's flow), the same builder agents bound to the same runners and models, the same mender model and the same project checks; the reviewer exists only at Gated. Each build's record, as the app shows it, names its base commit, level, builders and the model of every run.

The two builds run one after the other, Fast first, while no other flow or build runs in the project, no agent is building other work, and no leftover Hub or test process from an earlier drive is running on the machine.

Each build lands its approved work on its own branch cut from the base commit, never on master; no commit of either build reaches master until the operator chooses, after the comparison is recorded, which result to merge.

Each build runs under a budget cap of $30 API-equivalent and a window of 8 hours, and stops at either; a stopped build is recorded with its numbers as they stood and marked stopped, never restarted. If a build is blocked for over 30 minutes by a Hub defect rather than the change, it is stopped, a finding is filed, and both builds are re-run once after the fix from a common new base; a second such stop, or the measurement's total passing $65, ends it as inconclusive with what it found.

After each build ends, the candidate's acceptance criteria and every project check, the UI check included, are run on that build's landed branch by someone who took no part in the build, and each failure is counted as an escaped defect of that build.

The comparison measures re-recording held evidence over every send-back in the project since slice K shipped, the Gated build's included: held pieces recorded again, the review rounds that judged them again with their minutes and cost, and how many failed when judged again. It ends with a recommendation by this rule: carry held pieces forward when at least 5 were judged again, none failed, and those review rounds cost at least 10% of all review cost; keep re-recording when any failed; otherwise keep re-recording and say the evidence is too thin.

The comparison is one Markdown note added to the project's tracked vault as a 'document' source, dated the day it was written and distilled, so that it is listed in the Vault tab, its body and metadata are committed under knowledge/sources/, and its facts can be cited by the document that decides carrying forward.

requirement_links.statement: A document's header shows its phase and the actions open to it as buttons: Check while it is being written (never changing its phase), Approve when it is ready, Build or 'Approve and build' once it may be built, with the one the document is waiting for visually primary.
Pressing Check shows what blocks approval and what only warns, beside the parts of the document they concern, without leaving the page or freezing the document.
The document's sections, requirements, acceptance criteria and tasks are rendered by the app from the document's structure, so the page can filter, order, highlight and link them.

The document list can be filtered by kind, phase, text and 'has a build running', ordered by last change, phase, title or roadmap order, and grouped under its roadmap, and the choice persists per project.
Within a document, requirements can be filtered by evidence state and by task, and tasks by status and agent; tasks can be ordered by status or by build order (dependencies).

An outline of the open document jumps to any section, requirement or task; a slice links to its roadmap and to the previous and next slice; back and forward return to the previous position; every position has a link that reopens it.

Each build of the document shows, live: its driver, level and people; tasks by status; wall time split into building, waiting for review, checks and waiting to be handed out; runs; and cost split between building, reviewing and leading.
The conversation's spec side panel shows the same document, actions, navigation and build progress as the Spec tab, in a layout that fits the panel's width.

The page uses only the app's tokens and primitives, works in dark and light, animates state changes (opening, checking, a build's progress) with the motion tokens, and stops animating under reduced motion.
A mock of the Spec tab and the side panel, built from the real components fed recorded fixtures under hub/ui/mock, is approved by the operator before the page is wired to the Hub.

The side panel switches to any other document from a switcher above its tabs; jumps to any section, and to any requirement or task from a strip that shows each one's state, with previous and next and its position; and filters and orders from one tray whose active choices stay visible as chips that remove themselves one at a time or all at once.

Choosing a spec to open, from the panel's Specs tab, the Ctrl/Cmd+K picker or the panel's switcher, is one picker: a search field from which Enter opens the first match it names; with nothing typed, shortcuts to the conversation's attached document, to documents with a build running (with their progress) and to the last three opened; then every document with the Spec tab's filters, order and roadmap grouping. Opening never attaches a document to the conversation.

requirement_links.statement: The operator MUST be able to change the whole text of a text source from the Vault tab, tracked or private. The source keeps its id, name, type, visibility, dated and created_at; from the moment the change is answered, the map's opening and every read of the entry (operator's and agents') answer the new text.
Changing the text of a PDF or image source, by any of the ways to edit, MUST be refused with a reason saying the file is changed by replacing it, and change nothing.

The operator MUST be able to replace a PDF or image source's file from the Vault tab with a new file, subject to the same type and signature checks as an upload. The source keeps its id, name, type, visibility, dated and created_at; its file route answers the new bytes and its earlier transcription is discarded, so the next distillation transcribes the new file.

Every edit, replacement, archive and restore of a source MUST be recorded with the source: what was done, when, and who did it — the operator, or the agent's name and run id taken from the run's credential, never from the request. A read of the entry MUST answer its changes, oldest first, and the Vault tab MUST show them on the selected source. A tracked source's changes MUST be written under knowledge/ beside it.
When an edit or replacement is answered and the vault-distillation job is enabled with a runner, the Hub MUST distil the source again in the background; the answer MUST NOT wait for any model.

When an edit or replacement is made while the vault-distillation job is disabled or has no runner, the change MUST still be saved and answered, the answer saying the source's facts are stale and what to enable. Until a distillation of the source completes, each of its facts MUST be listed with stale true, and its vault_read content MUST say its source changed after it was drawn.

The operator's edit MUST name the version of the text it was made from, and MUST be refused, changing nothing, with a reason saying the source changed since it was opened, when the source's text is no longer that version.

tasks.notes: Reviewed 9d124d9 (test-only change). The fixed 1.5s sleep and the 7s wall-clock bound are replaced by a handshake: the older run's check touches a marker and holds until the test releases it. The completion is bounded by a 60s wait_for hang guard and must return 200 while the older run is still in flight. Release and drain happen in a finally. Nothing is quarantined, and the assertion still means what it did. Verified myself: the whole file passes (19 passed, 139s); ruff and black (py311) are clean. Defect injection: setting `asyncio.wait({job}, timeout=None)` in project_checks._stop_run_on_older_work, so the stop ignores the budget, made the target test fail with TimeoutError. requirement_links.statement: The commits that a task's completion check, review turn and approval check treat as the task's work are the task's own: the newest commit on its branch and commits named by evidence it recorded. A commit named by evidence another task recorded, including against a requirement both tasks serve and including after that task is approved, never counts as this task's work.

Every move of a task to completed, including each one after a send-back, either records a check run whose target contains that completion's newest branch commit, or says in the task's history why no check ran. It never skips silently because a stand-in commit is already on the main branch.

The work a dependent task's checkout takes in from a prerequisite, and the work approval requires the dependent's branch to contain, are commits produced by that prerequisite task. A commit produced by a task the dependent does not depend on, directly or through its prerequisites, is never required.
A 'Bring in prerequisite work' commit made by the Hub names the task that produced the commit it merges.
